subject: Physics
content: Coulomb's law: the electrostatic force between two point charges is directly proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance. F = k*q1*q2/r^2. Like charges repel, opposite attract. Electric field E is force per unit charge. Potential is work per unit charge to bring a charge from infinity.
analogy: Two like charges are like two students who've had a fight — push them closer and they shove apart harder. Opposite charges are like a crush — they pull toward each other.

subject: Physics
content: First law: energy is conserved. dU = Q - W, Q heat added, W work done by the system. Internal energy depends only on state. Isothermal: temperature constant. Adiabatic: no heat exchanged.
analogy: A pressure cooker: heat in (Q) either cooks the food (raises internal energy U) or pushes the whistle up (work W). Energy just changes form.

subject: Chemistry
content: At equilibrium the forward and backward reaction rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant. Le Chatelier: disturb the system and it shifts to counteract the change. Kc is the equilibrium constant.
analogy: A busy chai stall at a railway station: customers arrive and leave at the same rate, so the crowd size stays constant even as individuals come and go.

subject: Chemistry
content: A mole is 6.022e23 particles (Avogadro's number). Molar mass is grams per mole. Moles = mass / molar mass. Stoichiometry uses mole ratios from balanced equations.
analogy: A mole is a counting unit like 'a dozen' (12) — just an enormously big chemist's dozen. You don't count each egg in a dozen; chemists don't count each atom.

subject: Biology
content: Converts light energy to chemical energy. Light reactions in thylakoids make ATP and NADPH. Calvin cycle in the stroma fixes CO2 into glucose. 6CO2 + 6H2O + light -> C6H12O6 + 6O2.
analogy: A tiffin factory in the leaf: sunlight is the electricity (light reactions = energy), the Calvin cycle is cooks assembling raw CO2 into finished tiffins (glucose); oxygen is leftover packaging.

subject: Biology
content: The cell is the basic unit of life. Nucleus holds DNA and controls activities. Mitochondria make ATP. Ribosomes synthesize proteins. Membrane is selectively permeable. Plant cells add a wall and chloroplasts.
analogy: A cell is a coaching institute: nucleus = director's office (holds the master plan), mitochondria = canteen (energy), ribosomes = teachers (produce proteins), membrane = security gate.
